items.name: GJ 667 A

Effective temp (K).source: Santos et al. 2005, A&A 437, 1127 (2005A&A...437.1127S), as catalogued in PASTEL (VizieR B/pastel/pastel, entry HD 156384): Teff = 4819 +/- 110 K, logg 4.66, [Fe/H] -0.43
Effective temp (K).method: Spectroscopic (Santos+2005). TIC v8.2 adopts the same value for HD 156384 (r_Teff = spect).

items.reason: No Teff exists for GJ 667 A alone: A and B are 1.8 arcsec apart and every spectrum or SED is their combined light, dominated by A (about 1 mag brighter in V). The spectroscopic value with a stated error, which TIC v8.2 adopts, is Santos et al. 2005: 4819 +/- 110 K.
items.notes: Describes GJ 667 A, the row's own star (K3 V primary), measured in COMBINED A+B light (HD 156384 = GJ 667 AB). B (K5 V) pulls a blended Teff cooler, so A itself is probably no cooler than this. NOT the archive's 3350 K, which is GJ 667 C, the planet host. Published alternatives, all AB blends: Perrin et al. 1988 4941 K (PASTEL); PASTEL mean (Soubiran et al. 2022, A&A 663, A4, J/A+A/663/A4/meanpast) 4886 +/- 74 K from 2 values; AMBRE/FEROS automated 4653 K (J/A+A/690/A97) and 4645 K (J/A+A/704/A49); McDonald et al. 2017 SED 4651 K (J/MNRAS/471/770); Hardegree-Ullman et al. 2023 5032 +/- 383 K (photometric, J/AJ/165/267). The spread is 4645-5032 K, an uncertainty of about 150 K. I recommend 4819 because it is spectroscopic, has an error bar and is the value TIC adopts; a writer who prefers the most recent value could use AMBRE's 4653. CONSISTENCY FLAG: the Multi-stars GJ 667 A luminosity (0.173, orange) was derived with Teff = 4270 K (Johnson & Wright 1983), and every modern value is 400-750 K hotter. I did not open the Santos 2005 paper itself; the value comes from the PASTEL catalogue query.

Other published blended values: McDonald et al. 2017 SED 4388 K (J/MNRAS/471/770; also in HPIC), Oelkers et al. 2018 4415 K (J/AJ/155/39), Stevens et al. 2017 4492 K (J/AJ/154/259). The range is 4388-4492 K. Houdebine 2019 give spectral type sdK4.6 and used C's Gaia DR2 parallax (31.09 mas) for this pair; that affects only their radius, not the colour Teff.

items.name: psi1 Dra A

Effective temp (K).source: Endl et al. 2016, ApJ 818, 34 (arXiv:1512.02965), Table 10 row 3: psi1 Dra A Teff = 6544 +/- 42 K (strict differential analysis relative to psi1 Dra B)
Effective temp (K).method: Spectroscopic: Fe-line excitation/ionisation balance (MOOG), differential to B.

Host mass (M-sun).source: Casagrande et al. 2011, A&A 530, A138 (Geneva-Copenhagen re-analysis), VizieR J/A+A/530/A138/catalog, HIP 86614 (HD 162003, m_Name A): Padova Bayesian mass, median 1.44 M-sun (16-84%: 1.41-1.47); IRFM Teff 6542 K
Host mass (M-sun).method: Isochrone (Padova) Bayesian mass from IRFM Teff, [Fe/H] and Hipparcos parallax.

Gaia DR3 source_id.source: Gaia DR3 gaia_source (queried 2026-09-27) and SIMBAD ident (HD 162003 = Gaia DR3 1651268660203160448): plx 43.950 +/- 0.862 mas, G 4.444, BP-RP 0.608, RUWE 3.43; 29.9 arcsec from psi1 Dra B (1651268763282397312, plx 44.050)
Gaia DR3 source_id.method: SIMBAD cross-id, confirmed by position (0.4 arcsec from the row's RA/Dec), parallax (matches the Multi-stars note, 43.9499 mas) and brightness (the only G < 6 source in the field besides B).

items.reason: Endl et al. 2016 (Table 10) measured psi1 Dra A itself: Teff 6544 +/- 42 K (6546 +/- 56 K against the Sun). Endl et al. do not derive A's mass, so the mass comes from Casagrande et al. 2011: 1.44 M-sun.
items.notes: All values describe psi1 Dra A (HD 162003, HIP 86614), the row's own star, NOT the planet host psi1 Dra B (the archive values Teff 6212 K and M 1.19 are B's). TEFF: Endl 2016 Table 10 gives 6546 +/- 56 (Sun reference) and 6544 +/- 42 (B reference); their Casagrande colour calibration gives 6519 +/- 20. Others: Casagrande 2011 IRFM 6542, Luck 2017 6573 +/- 49 (J/AJ/153/21), Brewer et al. 2016 6411 (J/ApJS/225/32, also TIC). MASS: the sources span 1.19-1.48. Casagrande 2011 gives 1.44 (Padova) and 1.47 (BaSTI). Brewer 2016 gives an isochrone mass of 1.46 (1.43-1.52) but a spectroscopic-logg mass of 1.30 +/- 0.17. Endl 2016 Table 5 ADOPTS 1.430 for its A-C orbit fit and quotes Toyota et al. 2009 M_A ~1.38 in Sect. 5.2.2 (the Multi-stars A row has 1.38). Luck 2017 gives a mean of 1.26 and David & Hillenbrand 2015 give 1.19 (1.1-1.3; J/ApJ/804/146). I recommend 1.44 because it comes with a Teff (6542) that matches Endl's spectroscopic Teff and agrees with Endl's adopted 1.430 and Brewer's isochrone 1.46. CAVEAT: A is an SB1 with a stellar companion C (Endl 2016 Table 5: P = 6649 d, m sin i = 551 MJup ~0.53 M-sun, a = 8.7 AU), whose light could bias photometric masses slightly. GAIA: RUWE 3.43 and the 0.86 mas parallax error reflect the A-C orbit and the star's brightness (G 4.4). The brief asked for A's Gaia id and the cell is blank on this row, so I put it under the Gaia DR3 source_id header. The row's luminosity 2.21 is psi1 Dra B's (the planet host), as the column defines; I left it alone.

incidental_finds: Row numbers are not stable: my first read of Systems within 100 ly (2026-09-27) had GJ 237 at row 373, GJ 4248 at 376, GJ 65 at 377 and UPM J2155-2803 at 420; a later read matched the brief (49, 50, 55, 59, 66, 70, 118, 207, 245, 374, 418, 419, 420, 428). Key every write on the name or Gaia id.

GJ 237 row: Host mass 0.574 comes from TIC v8.2 with s_Mass = 1.507 M-sun (no constraint). Gaidos et al. 2014 (J/MNRAS/443/2561) give GJ 237 B 0.43 +/- 0.07 M-sun; Hardegree-Ullman 2023 give 0.575 +/- 0.575. Do not trust the 0.574.

GJ 667 A (Multi-stars): the orange-bordered luminosity 0.173 was derived with Teff = 4270 K (Johnson & Wright 1983). Every later spectroscopic or SED value for HD 156384 is 4645-4941 K (PASTEL, AMBRE, McDonald 2017); with R = 0.76 and Teff 4819 the same Stefan-Boltzmann derivation gives ~0.28, not 0.173. Worth re-checking.

GJ 65 B (Multi-stars): L 0.00149 (orange, from R = 0.159 and Teff 2842) vs the Hardegree-Ullman et al. 2023 bolometric 9.72e-4 for Gaia DR3 5140693571158946048 (J/AJ/165/267/table1). One of the two is off by 35%; B is 2 arcsec from A, so the Gaia photometry may be the problem.
GJ 4248: Kirkpatrick et al. 2024 (J/ApJS/271/55/table4) give optical type M3 V (Henry et al. 2018) against the sheet's M3.5V (SIMBAD, Reid 1995).

GJ 338 A/B: SIMBAD (A K7V, B M0V) and Kirkpatrick et al. 2024 Table 4 (A = HD 79210 M0 V, B = HD 79211 K7 V) swap the two Kirkpatrick 1991 types; CARMENES (Cifuentes 2020) give HD 79210 M0.0 V. The sheet has M0 V for both.

Gaia DR3 GSP-Spec Teff is unusable for M dwarfs at the grid edge: 4250 K for UPM J2155-2803, LSPM J2028+0524, UPM J0805-3522 and UPM J1831+6524 (run4/candidates.json), and 3132 K for GJ 4248 against 3241-3434 K from six papers.
UPM J0805-3522 is a candidate member of the ~210 Myr MELANGE-5 association (Thao et al. 2024, AJ 168, 41, J/AJ/168/41/table3). If it is young, its TIC main-sequence mass and radius may be off.
